chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Munzir ibn Yazeed, from Al-Mufazzal ibn Umar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When it is the Day of Judgment, a Caller will call out: “Where are the hinderers against My friends?” So a group will stand, there not being any flesh upon their faces, and it will be said: “These are the ones who hurt the believers, established hostility against them, were stubborn with them, and were violent with them regarding their religion.” Then they will be commanded to Hell.'

key_terms.الصُّدُودُ: The hinderers or those who obstructed

ai.seo_question: Who are the 'hinderers' (Al-Sudood) mentioned in the hadith regarding the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) describes the 'Suddud' (those who hindered) as a specific group on the Day of Judgment whose faces are emaciated, signifying the spiritual withering caused by their persistent hostility toward the faithful. This highlights the Shia concept of 'adhab al-barzakh' and eschatological retribution for those who actively opposed the believers' religious practice, distinguishing them from general disbelievers by their specific role in causing distress to the community.
